newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power stalled by delivery problems.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power stalled by delivery problems.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly steady Wednesday due to ongoing transmission constraints, industry sources said.

"Prices were up, but there was not a lot of business because they would have trouble going south," said one power marketer, referring to the transmission gluts out of the Tennessee Valley Authority's system and into the Southern Co's system.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices on Tennessee Valley Authority's system were unchanged at $17.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).
At the Georgia-Florida border, firm, peak electricity was valued in the $22.25-23.00 range, down from the $24.00-25.00 range seen on Tuesday.
The aftermath of Tropical Storm Josephine added to the sluggish activity and reluctance on the part of buyers as heavy rains and cooler weather dampened air-conditioning demand.
